findings.detail: The dev lane previously used `cancel-in-progress: false` with the note that a running run always completes. The head sets `cancel-in-progress: true` on group `release-dev-branch-dev`. The called release-provider.yml runs inside this caller's concurrency scope, so a second `workflow_dispatch` on `dev` cancels the whole in-flight run, including Developer ID signing, notarization, R2 staging and registration. Registration or staging can then be left half-finished, and each new run gets a new run_number version. Any repository writer can dispatch (no inputs, `github.ref == refs/heads/dev` is the only check) and can keep cancelling releases, or leave staged but unregistered artifacts. This replaces the push trigger, which only ledger-bypass accounts could fire. Fix: keep `cancel-in-progress: false` for the `dev` group, or cancel only before the signing and publish jobs. Restrict dispatch to authorized actors.
findings.title: Dev-branch signing/publish run can now be cancelled mid-flight by a later dispatch

findings.detail: The review job now runs only when the `run-threat-model` label is added (`types: [labeled]`, `if: ... github.event.label.name == 'run-threat-model'`). The old trigger covered opened/synchronize/reopened/edited, and the removed comment explained that in clearance mode an edited PR must not replace a failed required run with a skipped success. The workflow still supports `THREAT_REVIEW_REQUIRE_CLEARANCE=true` (continue-on-error, membership token and the `threat-review-gate.py after` step), so that mode remains in use. If it is enabled and the job is a required check, any push without a fresh label produces no run, or a skipped job that GitHub counts as satisfied. A later push to the head SHA can therefore merge without a new review or clearance evaluation, bypassing the review of provider/attestation-affecting code. Whether the gate is required is repo configuration not supplied here. Fix: in clearance mode, keep the synchronize/reopened triggers, or add an always-running gate job that fails unless a review or override exists for the current head SHA.
findings.title: Label-only trigger can turn the threat-review clearance gate into a skipped (passing) check on new pushes

findings.detail: The old `if` carried a comment that, in clearance mode, an edited PR must not replace a failed required run with a skipped success. The new `if` (line 71) only runs the job when the label is `run-threat-model`, and the trigger is now `types: [labeled]` (line 6). With THREAT_REVIEW_REQUIRE_CLEARANCE=true, any other label event on a new head SHA makes the `review` job skip, and GitHub treats a skipped job as a passing required check. A user with triage rights (or automation) could add an unrelated label after a push or a failed run, so a required threat-model check could show as skipped/green with no `threat-review-gate.py after` evaluation. Fix: when clearance is required, keep the job running for every event and fail or pend closed unless the run-threat-model label is present, or run the gate in a separate job that always executes. Whether this applies depends on how the required-check rule is configured, which is not visible here.
findings.title: Clearance mode: unrelated label now yields a skipped (passing) job in place of a clearance run
